text.p: Read-Rite Corp. Tuesday adopted an anti-takeover defence, a day after it rejected a $1.76 billion offer from Applied Magnetics Corp., another maker of computer disk drives.
Read-Rite said its board of directors approved a dividend distribution of one preferred share purchase right on each outstanding share of the company's common stock.

"The rights are designed to protect and maximize the long-term value of the company for our shareholders by assuring that they receive fair and equal treatment in any unsolicited proposed takeover of the company," Chairman Cyril Yansouni said in a statement.

Read-Rite, the world's largest independent supplier of recording heads, said on Monday that its board had voted unanimously to reject the Applied Magnetics offer and remain independent. In February Applied Magnetics offered 0.679 share of its common stock, worth about $36, for each Read-Rite share.

Under Read-Rite's plan, each right will entitle shareholders to buy one one-thousandth of a share of the company's series A preferred stock at an exercise price of $150. The Rights come into effect 10 days after a person or group acquires 20 percent or more of the company's common stock or starts a tender offer for 20 percent or more of the company.
